mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases when UNRATE < 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases by >5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% year-over-year indicates a strong economy, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases when GDPC1 growth > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is increasing, it indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: low unemployment and high employment growth
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS is increasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates increased supply and economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases by >2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month during a monetary tightening cycle indicates weaker demand, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases when RSAFS declines by >2% and FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5%, it indicates high inflation and tight monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases when CPIAUCSL increases by >3% and FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
